value.first: I'd go with iron-first solids with early-and-often allergen introduction. Two clocks are running: the iron he was born with runs low around now, and waiting on allergens doesn't protect, it backfires. At 6 months he's right on time if he sits upright with support from the chair, opens for food, and doesn't tongue it all back out. Day 1: a spoon or two of iron-fortified cereal or mashed lentils, upright in a high chair. Most ends up on the tray. That's a win.
value.second: Days 2-7: iron-rich food twice a day, plus veg and fruit; milk continues as usual. Week 2: peanut. In the morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter into a purée, give a tiny taste, wait 10 minutes, then the rest, and watch him for two hours. Next day or two: well-cooked egg, same routine. Then one allergen a day: yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, fish. Once tolerated, keep each about twice a week. No honey before 12 months.
value.third: Noisy gagging is normal and fades; refusal just means try another day. If you'd rather skip purees, baby-led weaning works with the same allergen schedule. Get lumpy and soft finger foods in by 9 months. If he gets a few hives, a spreading rash or vomits after a food, stop it and see your provider before offering it again. Emma Hubbard, a paediatric OT, has a good walkthrough. I'll check in Saturday.
